extraction.Name: Raymond Big Crow
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his allotment, as he did not want to pay taxes; but his faimer and the people at the Indian Agency advised him to take it, and he did so
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold it, in 1920, to Mr. Sam Pelley, of Oelrichs, South Dakota, receiving $500.00 in cash, the place being free from all encumbrance, including taxes
extraction.Buyer: Mr. Sam Pelley, of Oelrichs, South Dakota, for $500.00 in cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: did not want to continue paying taxes on this allotment, and sold it
extraction.Occupation/Income: only income is what he makes by renting his mothing place, receiving a share of what he raises
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, health in good condition; financial standing poor; only property is a few horses and other chattels; has never received any aid from the County or Government; has a wife, seven children and a step-son all depending upon him for support; health of entire family is good; he considers $500.00 was a fair price for the time, taking in account the quality of the land; document contains a pronoun inconsistency ('she is 35 years old' in the sworn statement but 'his' used throughout)
